questions.stem: A 45‑year‑old man presents with a purulent wound infection after a road traffic accident. Gram staining of the wound exudate shows gram‑positive cocci in chains. Which of the following organisms is the most likely cause of this infection?
questions.explanation: Streptococcus pyogenes (group A β‑hemolytic streptococci) are gram‑positive cocci in chains and are common causes of skin and soft tissue infections following trauma. Staphylococcus aureus appears in clusters, S. pneumoniae is a lancet‑shaped diplococcus, and Enterococcus faecalis is a gram‑positive coccus in chains but is more associated with urinary tract and intra‑abdominal infections.
questions.source: Basic principles of bacterial morphology and common wound pathogens
